sentences.text: 3 . Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is in jail since 20.05.2024.
As many as nine witnesses have been examined.
Dying declaration has been taken as Exhibit-P/10 and the suicide note has been seized.
In respect of suicide note, handwriting expert's report has been called by the prosecution though, it is positive in that regard, but identity of present is not established by the prosecution.
It is also submitted that the Tahsildar, who has taken the dying declaration has admitted in his cross-examination that the women may commit suicide for various reasons.
No criminal act has been committed by the appellant herein by instigating the prosecutrix/deceased to commit suicide.
In respect of the allegations made against the appellant, as to commit rape neither the DNA report nor the FSL report has been called for.
He has no criminal antecedents.

sentences.text: 1 interrogation is required in the matter.
The conclusion of the trial will take time.
He is ready and willing to abide by all the terms and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
In view of the aforesaid, learned counsel for the appellant prays for grant of bail to the appellant.

4 . Per contra,
learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the objector have vehemently opposed the bail application/appeal, contending that the statements of as many as nine prosecution witnesses, along with other documentary evidence on record, clearly incriminate the appellant.
It is submitted that the dying declaration (Exhibit-P/10) as well as the suicide note categorically disclose that the present appellant committed rape upon the prosecutrix and, being a photographer,
continuously

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9320 3 CRA-900-2025 blackmailed her,
which ultimately drove the prosecutrix to commit suicide.
In view of the aforesaid, he has prayed for rejection of this appeal for bail.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

6 . Having regard to the nature and gravity of the allegations, the specific role attributed to the appellant, the evidence available on record, and without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the considered view that no case for grant of bail is made out at this stage.

7. Accordingly, the appeal for bail is hereby dismissed.
(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE julie Shravan@Shi@Shivruddh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24730174/
